questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements about biomolecules.
A. Lipids are generally water soluble.
B. Proteins are polypeptides.
C. Polysaccharides are long chains of sugars.
D. Adenine and guanine are substituted pyrimidines.
E. Almost all enzymes are proteins.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because lipids are generally water insoluble.

Statement B is correct because proteins are polypeptides, which are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

Statement C is correct because polysaccharides are long chains of sugars (monosaccharides).

Statement D is incorrect because adenine and guanine are substituted purines, whereas cytosine, uracil, and thymine are substituted pyrimidines.

Statement E is correct because almost all enzymes are proteins, with a few exceptions like ribozymes (which are nucleic acids).

Therefore, the correct statements are B, C, and E.

Answer: B, C and E only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The amino acid that gives a red-blood colour on treating its sodium fusion extract with sodium nitroprusside is
questions.solution:
Methionine is the only amino acid among the given options that contains sulphur.

During sodium fusion, an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur forms sodium thiocyanate ($NaSCN$).

This extract gives a blood-red colour when treated with $Fe^{3+}$ ions due to the formation of ferric thiocyanate, $[Fe(SCN)]^{2+}$.

Although the question mentions sodium nitroprusside (which typically yields a violet colour with sulphide ions), the blood-red colour specifically confirms the presence of both nitrogen and sulphur. Therefore, methionine is the correct choice.

Answer: methionine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids ?
A. They are substituted methanes.
B. Serine is an aromatic amino acid.
C. Valine is a neutral amino acid.
D. Lysine is an acidic amino acid.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same carbon, i.e., the $\alpha$-carbon. Therefore, they are considered substituted methanes. Statement A is correct.

Serine contains a hydroxymethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$) as its side chain and is an aliphatic amino acid, not an aromatic one. Aromatic amino acids include phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan. Statement B is incorrect.

Valine contains one amino group and one carboxyl group, making it a neutral amino acid. Statement C is correct.

Lysine contains two amino groups and one carboxyl group, making it a basic amino acid, not an acidic one. Acidic amino acids include aspartic acid and glutamic acid. Statement D is incorrect.

Thus, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The protein portion of an enzyme is called:
questions.solution:
There are number of cases in which non-protein constituents called co-factors are bound to the enzyme to make the enzyme catalytically active.

In these instances, the protein portion of the enzymes is called the apoenzyme.
Three kinds of co-factors are identified prosthetic groups, co-enzymes and metal ions. Prosthetic groups are organic compounds and they are tightly bound with apoenzyme. Co-enzymes are also organic compounds but their association with apoenzyme is only transient.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct statement about peptides and proteins is
options: In $\alpha$-helices, the polypeptide chain is twisted into a left-handed screw (helix) through intramolecular hydrogen bonds.
Tertiary structure of proteins has two or more polypeptide subunits.
Only the proteins having a quaternary structure are biologically active.
In $\beta$-pleated sheet structures, peptide chains are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
questions.solution:
In $\alpha$-helix structure, the polypeptide chain is twisted into a right-handed screw, not left-handed.

Tertiary structure represents the overall folding of a single polypeptide chain. Proteins with two or more polypeptide subunits exhibit quaternary structure.

Proteins can be biologically active in their tertiary structure as well, so it is incorrect to say only proteins with quaternary structure are active.

In $\beta$-pleated sheet structures, all peptide chains are stretched out to nearly maximum extension and laid side by side, held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Answer: In $\beta$-pleated sheet structures, peptide chains are held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds can form a zwitter ion?
questions.solution:
The molecule which forms zwitter ion is glycine.

Every zwitterion has an isoelectric point (pI). The isoelectric point is the pH at which a zwitterion is uncharged. The pH can affect the charge of a molecule by introducing protons (H+). The amino group of an amino acid is a very effective proton acceptor, so is considered to be basic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure ?
questions.solution:
The primary structure of a protein refers to the linear sequence of amino acids.

The secondary structure refers to the local folded structures that form within a polypeptide due to interactions between atoms of the backbone. The most common types of secondary structures are the $\alpha$-helix and the $\beta$-pleated sheet.

The tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional structure of a polypeptide.

The quaternary structure is the arrangement of multiple folded protein or coiling protein molecules in a multi-subunit complex.

Therefore, the $\alpha$-helix is found in the secondary structure of proteins.

Answer: Secondary structure

questions.q:
Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyzes the following reaction:

$\begin{array}{cc} X & Y \\ | & | \\ C & - & C \end{array} \rightarrow X-Y + C=C$
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 117 | Paragraph: 6

The given reaction involves the removal of groups $X$ and $Y$ from the substrate, resulting in the formation of a double bond between the carbon atoms.

Enzymes that catalyze the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds, are classified as lyases.

Hydrolases catalyze the cleavage of bonds by the addition of water.

Isomerases catalyze the interconversion of optical, geometric, or positional isomers.

Ligases catalyze the joining together of two molecules.

Thus, the enzyme catalyzing the given reaction belongs to the class lyase.

Answer: (2) Lyase

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ketoses give Seliwanoff’s test faster than Aldoses.

Reason (R): Ketoses undergo $\beta$-elimination followed by formation of furfural.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Seliwanoff 's test is a differentiating test for Ketose and aldose. This test relies on the principle that the keto hexose are more rapidly dehydrated to form $5$-hydroxy methyl furfural when heated in acidic medium which on condensation with resorcinol, Cherry red or brown red coloured complex is formed rapidly indicating a positive test. 

Aldoses take longer time to produce colour because under the same conditions, aldoses form furfural slowly, probably because β-elimination is required before dehydration to furfural. Therefore prolonged heating should be avoided.

Hence, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion (A): The denaturation of proteins can destroy all $1 ° , 2 °$ and $3 °$ protein structures.

Reason (R): Curdling of milk is due to denaturation of proteins.

The correct option among the following is
options: (A) is true, (R) is true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
(A) is true, (R) is true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
questions.solution:
Protein found in a biological system with a unique three-dimensional structure and biological activity is called a native protein. When a protein in its native form, is subjected to physical change like change in temperature or chemical change like change in pH, the hydrogen bonds are disturbed. Due to this, globules unfold and helix get uncoiled and protein loses its biological activity. This is called denaturation of protein.

The coagulation of egg white on boiling is a common example of denaturation. Another example is curdling of milk which is caused due to the formation of lactic acid by the bacteria present in milk.

During denaturation secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed but primary structure remains intact.

Hence,(A) is false but (R) is true

questions.q:
Observe the following statements.
I. Sucrose has glycosidic linkage.
II. Cellulose is present in both plants and animals.
III. Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units.
Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let's evaluate each statement to determine which are correct.
- Statement I: Sucrose has a glycosidic linkage. This is correct. Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by a glycosidic linkage between a glucose unit and a fructose unit.
- Statement II: Cellulose is present in both plants and animals. This is incorrect. Cellulose is the main structural component of the primary cell wall of green plants, but it's not present in animals. Animals lack the enzyme cellulase to break down cellulose.
- Statement III: Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units. This is correct. Lactose is a disaccharide commonly known as milk sugar. It's composed of one molecule of Dgalactose and one molecule of D-glucose, joined by a \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic linkage.
Therefore, the correct statements are I and III. The correct option is (4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
a) In maltose, C-1 of one $\alpha-\mathrm{D}$-glucose is linked to $\mathrm{C}-4$ of second $\alpha-\mathrm{D}$-glucose
b) Quaternary structure of protein represents spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide chains with respect to each other
c) Nucleotide units in a nucleic acid are joined to each other through a phosphodiester linkage
d) Abnormally low level of thyroxine leads to hypothyroidism
questions.solution:
- a) In maltose, \($\mathrm{C}-$1\) of one \($\alpha-\mathrm{D}$\)-glucose is linked to \($\mathrm{C}-$4\) of a second \($\alpha-\mathrm{D}$\)-glucose. This is the defining structure of maltose, a disaccharide. The bond between the two glucose units is an \($\alpha-$1,4\)-glycosidic linkage.
- b) Quaternary structure of a protein represents the spatial arrangement of two or more polypeptide chains with respect to each other. This is the correct definition of the quaternary structure of a protein. It describes how multiple protein subunits interact and arrange themselves to form a larger functional complex.
- c) Nucleotide units in a nucleic acid are joined to each other through a phosphodiester linkage. In DNA and RNA, the backbone is formed by alternating sugar and phosphate groups linked together. The bond that connects the \(3^{\prime}\) carbon of one sugar to the \(5^{\prime}\) carbon of the next is a phosphodiester bond.
- d) Abnormally low levels of thyroxine lead to hypothyroidism. Thyroxine (\(T_4\)) is a hormone produced by the thyroid gland. A deficiency of this hormone causes the metabolic disorder known as hypothyroidism, which is characterized by a slow metabolism, weight gain, and fatigue.
Since all statements are accurate, the correct option is (2) \($\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{d}$\).

- b. The sources of vitamin \(B_2\) are milk and liver. This statement is correct. Vitamin \(B_2\), also known as riboflavin, is found in a variety of foods, with rich sources including dairy products like milk and organ meats like liver.

The adrenal cortex produces glucocorticoids, such as cortisol, which help regulate blood sugar levels by promoting gluconeogenesis. Hypofunction of the adrenal cortex, as see in Addison's disease, leads to a deficiency of these hormones, which can result in a dangerously low blood glucose level, or hypoglycemia.

(i) Monosaccharides can be hydrolysed.
(ii) The two monosaccharide units obtained on hydrolysis of a disaccharide can either be same or different.

e.g., Sucrose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Fructose
Maltose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Glucose
So, statement (ii) is true.
(iii) Polysaccharides are polymers of many monosaccharides and have no sweet taste.
So, statements (iii) is true.
(iv) Monosaccharides are categorised as reducing and non-reducing sugars.
So, statement (iv) is not true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The incorrect statements regarding enzymes are :
(A) Enzymes are biocatalysts.
(B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions.
(C) Most Enzymes are globular proteins.
(D) Enzyme - oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution:
- (A) Enzymes are biocatalysts. This statement is correct. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms without being consumed in the process.
- (B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions. This statement is incorrect. Enzymes are highly specific in their action. Each enzyme typically catalyzes only one or a very small number of specific reactions due to its unique threedimensional shape, which fits a particular substrate.
- (C) Most enzymes are globular proteins. This statement is correct. The majority of enzymes are globular proteins, which means they are spherical or globe-like in shape. Their specific three-dimensional structure, including the active site, is crucial for their catalytic function.
- (D) Enzyme - oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose. This statement is incorrect. The enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of maltose is maltase, not oxidase. Oxidase enzymes catalyze oxidation-reduction reactions, not hydrolysis. The hydrolysis of maltose breaks it down into two glucose molecules.

  List-I   List-II
A Glucose $+ HI$ I Gluconic acid
B Glucose $+ {Br}_{2}$ water II Glucose pentacetate
C Glucose $+$ acetic anhydride III Saccharic acid
D Glucose $+ {HNO}_{3}$ IV Hexane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation:
A) On prolonged heating with HI, Glucose forms n-hexane, suggesting that all the six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.

B) Glucose gets oxidised to six carbon carboxylic acid (gluconic acid) on reaction with a mild oxidising agent like bromine water. This indicates that the carbonyl group is present as an aldehydic group.

C) Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate which confirms the presence of five –OH groups. Since it exists as a stable compound, five –OH groups should be attached to different carbon atoms.

 

D) On oxidation with nitric acid, glucose as well as gluconic acid both yield a dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid. This indicates the presence of a primary alcoholic (–OH) group in glucose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes protein denaturation from protein hydrolysis?
options: Denaturation breaks peptide bonds to unfold the protein, while hydrolysis breaks hydrogen bonds to yield free amino acids.
Both processes destroy the primary structure of the protein, but only hydrolysis yields free amino acids.
Denaturation alters the sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain, while hydrolysis only unfolds the secondary and tertiary structures.
Denaturation disrupts hydrogen bonds while leaving the primary structure intact, whereas hydrolysis breaks peptide bonds and destroys the primary structure.
questions.solution:
Denaturation of a protein is caused by physical or chemical changes (like heating or pH change) that disturb the hydrogen bonds. This destroys the secondary and tertiary structures, but the primary structure (the sequence of amino acids) remains intact.

In contrast, hydrolysis of a protein involves the chemical cleavage of the covalent peptide bonds that link the amino acids together, thereby destroying the primary structure and ultimately yielding free amino acids.

Answer: Denaturation disrupts hydrogen bonds while leaving the primary structure intact, whereas hydrolysis breaks peptide bonds and destroys the primary structure.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding enzyme classes and their functions.

List-IList-II
(A) Transferases(I) Linking together of 2 compounds
(B) Hydrolases(II) Hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide bonds
(C) Isomerases(III) Transfer of a group (other than hydrogen)
(D) Ligases(IV) Inter-conversion of optical, geometric or positional isomers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the IUBMB system of enzyme classification:

Transferases catalyse the transfer of a group (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates. Hence, (A) matches with (III).

Hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide or P-N bonds. Hence, (B) matches with (II).

Ligases catalyse the linking together of 2 compounds (e.g., joining of C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O bonds). Hence, (D) matches with (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Pernicious anaemia (where red blood cells are deficient in haemoglobin) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Adult human haemoglobin consists of four subunits, specifically two subunits of $\alpha$ type and two subunits of $\beta$ type. This assembly of multiple polypeptides represents which level of protein structure?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, some proteins are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or subunits. The manner in which these individual folded polypeptides or subunits are arranged with respect to each other is the architecture of a protein otherwise called the quaternary structure.

Adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits (two $\alpha$ and two $\beta$ type), which is a classic example of quaternary structure.

The $\alpha$ and $\beta$ designations here refer to the types of subunits in the quaternary assembly, not to the $\alpha$-helix or $\beta$-pleated sheet of the secondary structure.

Answer: Quaternary structure

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A molecule is formed by the attachment of the nitrogenous base uracil to the $1'$ position of a pentose sugar, which is further linked to phosphoric acid at its $5'$ position. Identify the pentose sugar present and the overall classification of the molecule.
questions.solution:
Uracil is a pyrimidine base found exclusively in RNA. Therefore, the pentose sugar it attaches to must be $\beta$-D-ribose, not $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose (which is found in DNA).

A nucleoside is formed when a base is attached to the $1'$ position of a sugar. When this nucleoside is further linked to phosphoric acid at the $5'$ position of the sugar moiety, it forms a nucleotide. Since the sugar is ribose and the phosphate group is present, the entire molecule is classified as a ribonucleotide.

Answer: $\beta$-D-ribose and Ribonucleotide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A researcher heats an aqueous solution of a globular protein. Upon analysis, it is observed that the protein has lost its biological activity and its helical structures have uncoiled, but the sequence of amino acids remains perfectly intact. Identify the phenomenon that has occurred and the primary type of bond that was disrupted during this process.
questions.solution:
When a protein is subjected to physical changes such as heating, the hydrogen bonds holding the secondary and tertiary structures are disturbed. This causes the uncoiling of helices and unfolding of globules, leading to a loss of biological activity.

This phenomenon is known as denaturation. Since the sequence of amino acids remains intact, the primary structure is preserved, which means the covalent peptide bonds are not broken during this process. Therefore, the phenomenon is denaturation and the disrupted bonds are hydrogen bonds.

Answer: Denaturation and Hydrogen bonds

questions.q: All $\alpha$-amino acids have a general formula $\text{R}-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ (except proline). If the side chain $\text{R}$ is $-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$, identify the correct name and the nature of the amino acid.
questions.solution:
The given side chain is $\text{R} = -\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$. Substituting this into the general formula $\text{R}-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{COOH}$ gives the structure of Aspartic acid.

Because the molecule contains two carboxyl ($-\text{COOH}$) groups and only one amino ($-\text{NH}_2$) group, it has more acidic groups than basic groups. Therefore, it is classified as an acidic amino acid.

Glutamic acid has the side chain $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$. Asparagine has the side chain $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CONH}_2$ and is neutral.

Answer: Aspartic acid, Acidic

questions.q:
Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyzes the following reaction :

S reduced + S' oxidised $\rightarrow$ S oxidised + S' reduced
questions.solution:
Enzymes which catalyse oxidoreduction between two substrates S and S' are known as oxidoreductases or dehydrogenases. The reaction is represented as:
S reduced + S' oxidised $\rightarrow$ S oxidised + S' reduced

Transferases catalyse the transfer of a group (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates.

Isomerases catalyse the interconversion of optical, geometric or positional isomers.

Lyases catalyse the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds.

Answer: Oxidoreductase

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true about naturally occurring fructose?
questions.solution:
Fructose is an important ketohexose. It contains six carbon atoms and a ketonic functional group at carbon number 2, making it a ketohexose.

Naturally occurring fructose belongs to the D-series and is a laevorotatory compound. It is appropriately written as D-(-)-fructose.

All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars. Fructose reduces Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution (under alkaline conditions, it isomerises to a mixture of glucose and mannose). Therefore, the statement that it is a non-reducing sugar is incorrect.

Answer: It is a non-reducing sugar.

questions.q: An enzyme isolated from a cell is found to catalyse the linking together of two compounds by specifically forming a P-O (phosphorus-oxygen) bond. According to the IUBMB system of enzyme classification, this enzyme belongs to which of the following classes?
questions.solution:
According to the IUBMB system of enzyme classification, enzymes that catalyse the linking together of two compounds are classified as ligases.

Ligases specifically catalyse the joining of bonds such as C-O, C-S, C-N, and P-O bonds. Therefore, an enzyme that forms a P-O bond to link two compounds is a ligase.

Lyases catalyse the removal of groups leaving double bonds, hydrolases catalyse bond cleavage using water, and transferases catalyse the transfer of a group from one substrate to another.

Answer: Ligases

questions.solution:
The complete catalytically active enzyme together with its bound non-protein constituent is called the holoenzyme (X).

The non-protein constituents that are bound to the enzyme to make it catalytically active are called cofactors (Y).

Answer: (X) - Holoenzyme, (Y) - Cofactor, (Z) - Apoenzyme

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A protein found in a biological system with a unique three-dimensional structure and biological activity is subjected to a significant change in pH, causing it to lose its biological activity.

What is the term used for the protein in its original active state, and which of its structural levels remains intact after the pH change?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, a protein found in a biological system with a unique three-dimensional structure and biological activity is called a native protein.

When a native protein is subjected to a physical change (like temperature) or a chemical change (like a change in pH), it undergoes denaturation. During denaturation, the protein loses its biological activity because the secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed (globules unfold and helices uncoil).

However, the primary structure (the specific sequence of amino acids held together by peptide bonds) remains intact during this process.

Answer: Native protein and Primary structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the denaturation of proteins:
I. Denaturation can be caused by physical changes like temperature or chemical changes like pH.
II. During this process, the uncoiling of helix and unfolding of globule takes place.
III. The primary structure of the protein is altered during the coagulation of egg white on boiling.
IV. Denaturation leads to the loss of biological activity of the protein.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: Denaturation is caused by physical changes (such as heating) or chemical changes (such as a change in pH) that disrupt the native conformation of the protein.

Statement II is correct: Denaturation involves the unfolding of globules and uncoiling of helices, which destroys the secondary and tertiary structures.

Statement III is incorrect: The coagulation of egg white on boiling is an example of denaturation. During denaturation, the primary structure remains intact and is not altered.

Statement IV is correct: The structural changes during denaturation lead to the loss of biological activity of the protein.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

According to NCERT, the primary structure of a protein provides positional information in a protein, which is the sequence of amino acids.

A protein is imagined as a line, where the left end represents the first amino acid and the right end represents the last amino acid.

The first amino acid is also called the N-terminal amino acid, and the last amino acid is called the C-terminal amino acid.

Therefore, the right end of the line represents the last amino acid, which is the C-terminal amino acid.

Answer: Last amino acid and is called the C-terminal amino acid

B. NucleotideII. $\beta$-D-ribose
C. Dinucleotide linkageIII. Base attached at $1'$ position of sugar

questions.solution:
A nucleoside is formed when a nitrogenous base is attached to the $1'$ position of a pentose sugar. (A $\rightarrow$ III)

Two nucleotides are joined together by a phosphodiester linkage between the $5'$ and $3'$ carbon atoms of the pentose sugar to form a dinucleotide. (C $\rightarrow$ I)

The pentose sugar present in RNA is $\beta$-D-ribose, whereas in DNA it is $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose. (D $\rightarrow$ II)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following options correctly represents the sequence of a nitrogenous base, its corresponding nucleoside, and its corresponding nucleotide, in that exact order?
questions.solution:
A nitrogenous base is a heterocyclic compound (e.g., Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, Uracil, Thymine).

When a nitrogenous base is attached to a pentose sugar, it forms a nucleoside (e.g., Guanosine, Thymidine).

When a phosphate group is esterified to the sugar of a nucleoside, it forms a nucleotide (e.g., Guanylic acid, Uridylic acid).

Therefore, the correct sequence is Guanine (base), Guanosine (nucleoside), and Guanylic acid (nucleotide).

Glycine is an amino acid, not a nitrogenous base. Thymine, Thymidine, and Uridylic acid do not form a corresponding sequence because Uridylic acid is a nucleotide of Uracil, not Thymine.

Answer: Guanine, Guanosine, Guanylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider a particular vitamin that is classified as water-soluble. Unlike most water-soluble vitamins, it is an exception because it can be stored in the human body (specifically in the liver). Furthermore, its primary dietary sources include meat, fish, egg, and curd. Identify this vitamin.
questions.solution:
Vitamins are classified into fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble (B group and C) vitamins.

Water-soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in the diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored in our body. A notable exception is Vitamin B$_{12}$, which is water-soluble but can be stored in the liver.

The primary dietary sources of Vitamin B$_{12}$ are animal products and microorganisms, specifically meat, fish, egg, and curd.

Vitamin C and Vitamin B$_{1}$ are water-soluble but cannot be stored in the body. Vitamin A can be stored in the liver but is a fat-soluble vitamin.

Answer: Vitamin B$_{12}$

questions.q: Which of the following generic reactions correctly represents the catalytic action of the enzyme class Oxidoreductases (dehydrogenases)?
options: $S \text{ reduced} + S' \text{ oxidised} \rightarrow S \text{ oxidised} + S' \text{ reduced}$
$S \text{ oxidised} + S' \text{ oxidised} \rightarrow S \text{ reduced} + S' \text{ reduced}$
questions.solution:
Enzymes are divided into 6 classes. Oxidoreductases (or dehydrogenases) are enzymes which catalyse oxidoreduction between two substrates S and S'.

The generic reaction for this class is represented as:
$S \text{ reduced} + S' \text{ oxidised} \rightarrow S \text{ oxidised} + S' \text{ reduced}$

The reaction $S - G + S' \rightarrow S + S' - G$ represents the action of Transferases, which transfer a group 'G' between substrates.

The reaction $X-C-C-Y \rightarrow X-Y + C=C$ represents the action of Lyases, which remove groups leaving double bonds.

The reaction showing both substrates oxidised converting to both reduced is chemically flawed and does not represent any enzyme class.

Answer: $S \text{ reduced} + S' \text{ oxidised} \rightarrow S \text{ oxidised} + S' \text{ reduced}$

questions.solution:

Therefore, the P-N bond is the correct answer as it is not joined by ligases.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the structure of a nucleotide that is found exclusively in DNA?
options: A unit containing thymine attached to the $1'$ position of $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, which is further linked to phosphoric acid at the $5'$ position.
A unit containing uracil attached to the $1'$ position of $\beta$-D-ribose, which is further linked to phosphoric acid at the $5'$ position.
A unit containing thymine attached to the $1'$ position of $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, which is further linked to phosphorous acid at the $5'$ position.
A unit containing thymine attached to the $5'$ position of $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, which is further linked to phosphoric acid at the $1'$ position.
questions.solution:
A nucleotide is formed when a nitrogenous base is attached to the $1'$ position of a pentose sugar, and phosphoric acid is linked to the $5'$ position of the sugar.

DNA exclusively contains the nitrogenous base thymine (whereas RNA contains uracil) and the pentose sugar $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose (whereas RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose).

Therefore, a nucleotide found exclusively in DNA consists of thymine attached to the $1'$ position of $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, with phosphoric acid linked at the $5'$ position.

Option 2 describes an RNA nucleotide. Option 3 incorrectly states phosphorous acid instead of phosphoric acid. Option 4 incorrectly swaps the attachment positions of the base and the phosphate group.

Answer: A unit containing thymine attached to the $1'$ position of $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, which is further linked to phosphoric acid at the $5'$ position.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In proteins, only right-handed helices are observed.
Reason (R): Secondary structure of protein refers to the local folding of the polypeptide chain into structures like helices.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in proteins, only right-handed helices are observed. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The secondary structure of a protein indeed refers to the local folding of the polypeptide chain, with the $\alpha$-helix being a prominent example. Thus, the Reason is also correct.

However, the general definition of secondary structure does not explain why only right-handed helices are formed (which is due to the stereochemistry of the constituent amino acids). Therefore, both statements are correct, but the Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Prosthetic group(I) Transient association with apoenzyme
(B) Co-enzyme(II) Tightly bound organic compound
(C) Metal ion(III) Zinc in carboxypeptidase
(D) Apoenzyme(IV) Protein portion of the enzyme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Based on the classification of cofactors in enzymes:

(A) Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. Hence, (A) matches with (II).

(B) Co-enzymes are also organic compounds but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis. Hence, (B) matches with (I).

(C) Metal ions form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate. Zinc is a metal ion cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase. Hence, (C) matches with (III).

(D) The protein portion of the enzyme is called the apoenzyme. Hence, (D) matches with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: To confirm the presence of hydroxyl groups in its structure, one mole of open-chain D-glucose is reacted with an excess of acetic anhydride. How many moles of acetic anhydride are consumed in this reaction, and what is the name of the derivative formed?
questions.solution:
The open-chain structure of D-glucose contains one aldehyde group and five hydroxyl (-OH) groups.

When reacted with acetic anhydride, acetylation occurs at each of the hydroxyl groups. Since there are five hydroxyl groups, one mole of glucose reacts with five moles of acetic anhydride.

The product formed is glucose pentaacetate, which confirms the presence of five -OH groups attached to different carbon atoms.

Answer: 5 moles, Glucose pentaacetate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A research team is designing an orally active analog of insulin for diabetic patients. To prevent the destruction of its primary structure by the enzymes present in the stomach and intestine, which specific type of chemical bond must primarily be protected from hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
Insulin is a proteinaceous hormone. The primary structure of proteins is formed by amino acids linked together by peptide bonds.

When administered orally, the proteolytic enzymes (proteases) in the gastrointestinal tract hydrolyse these peptide bonds, breaking down the hormone into inactive amino acids and destroying its biological activity. Therefore, to make insulin orally active, its peptide bonds would need to be protected from enzymatic hydrolysis.

Disulfide bonds link the two polypeptide chains (A and B) of insulin but are not the primary targets of digestive proteases. Glycosidic and phosphodiester bonds are found in carbohydrates and nucleic acids, respectively.

Answer: Peptide bonds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following deficiency diseases is caused by the specific water-soluble vitamin that is an exception because it can be stored in the human body?
questions.solution:
Water-soluble vitamins (B group and Vitamin C) are generally excreted in urine and cannot be stored in the body.

However, Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ is a notable exception as it is a water-soluble vitamin that can be stored in the liver.

According to NCERT, the deficiency of Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ causes pernicious anaemia, a condition where red blood cells are deficient in haemoglobin.

Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C (water-soluble, not stored), Beri-beri by Vitamin $\text{B}_{1}$ (water-soluble, not stored), and Night blindness by Vitamin A (fat-soluble).

Answer: Pernicious anaemia

Assertion (A): The enzyme class Lyase catalyses the removal of groups from substrates leaving double bonds.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.solution:

Statement II is incorrect because enzymes act as biocatalysts by providing an alternate pathway with a lower activation energy. They reduce, rather than increase, the magnitude of activation energy required for a biochemical reaction to proceed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following biochemical reactions:

[X] + Deoxyribose sugar $\rightarrow$ [Y]
[Y] + Phosphate group $\rightarrow$ [Z]

Identify X, Y, and Z correctly from the given options.
options: X = Thiamine, Y = Thymidine, Z = Thymidylic acid
X = Thymine, Y = Thymidine, Z = Thymidylic acid
X = Thymine, Y = Thymidylic acid, Z = Thymidine
X = Uracil, Y = Uridine, Z = Uridylic acid
questions.solution:
The given reactions describe the formation of a nucleotide from its components.

A nitrogenous base [X] combines with a pentose sugar to form a nucleoside [Y]. Since the sugar is explicitly given as deoxyribose, the base [X] can be Thymine (which is found in DNA), but not Uracil (which is found in RNA and pairs with ribose sugar).

Thymine [X] combines with deoxyribose sugar to form the nucleoside Thymidine [Y].

When a phosphate group is attached to the nucleoside Thymidine, it forms the nucleotide Thymidylic acid [Z].

Thiamine is a vitamin, not a nitrogenous base, making the first option incorrect. Swapping the nucleoside and nucleotide makes the third option incorrect.

Answer: X = Thymine, Y = Thymidine, Z = Thymidylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement regarding the properties of enzymes.
options: Enzymes increase the activation energy of biochemical processes to accelerate them.
Enzymes are primarily composed of complex polysaccharides.
Enzymes act as biocatalysts and are required only in very small quantities.
A single enzyme can efficiently catalyze many unrelated biochemical reactions.
questions.solution:
Enzymes are biocatalysts that are required in very small quantities to catalyze biochemical reactions.

The other statements are incorrect because:
- Enzymes lower (not increase) the activation energy of biochemical processes.
- Almost all enzymes are globular proteins, not polysaccharides.
- Enzymes are highly specific; a particular enzyme generally catalyzes only one specific reaction or acts on a specific substrate.

Answer: Enzymes act as biocatalysts and are required only in very small quantities.

questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: Cytosine is a pyrimidine nitrogenous base.
Statement II: Cytidine is a nucleotide formed by linking cytosine to a pentose sugar.
Statement III: Cytidylic acid is a nucleoside containing a phosphate group.
Statement IV: Cysteine is a sulphur-containing amino acid.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. Cytosine is a pyrimidine nitrogenous base found in nucleic acids.

Statement II is incorrect. Cytidine is a nucleoside, not a nucleotide. A nucleoside is formed when a nitrogenous base is linked to a pentose sugar.

Statement III is incorrect. Cytidylic acid is a nucleotide, not a nucleoside. It is formed when a phosphate group is esterified to the sugar of the nucleoside cytidine.

Statement IV is correct. Cysteine is an amino acid that contains sulphur in its side chain.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only two

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the curding of milk, the primary structure of milk proteins remains intact.

Reason (R): Curding of milk is caused by bacteria due to the formation of lactic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Curding of milk is an example of denaturation of proteins. During denaturation, the secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed, but the primary structure remains intact. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true.

Curding of milk is indeed caused by bacteria due to the formation of lactic acid, which lowers the pH and triggers denaturation. Therefore, Reason (R) is true.

However, Reason (R) explains the chemical cause of the curding process, not why the primary structure remains intact. The primary structure remains intact because denaturation disrupts only the weaker bonds (like hydrogen bonds) stabilizing higher structures, but does not break the covalent peptide bonds between amino acids. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oral contraceptive pills containing estrogen and progesterone are highly effective when taken orally, whereas insulin for diabetes management must be administered via injection. What is the primary biochemical basis for this difference in the route of administration?
options: Insulin is a steroid hormone that is poorly absorbed, while oral contraceptives are easily absorbed proteins.
Insulin is rapidly excreted by the kidneys if taken orally, whereas oral contraceptives are retained in the blood.
Oral contraceptives elicit a weaker immune response in the gut compared to oral insulin.
Insulin is a peptide hormone susceptible to digestion by gastrointestinal proteases, whereas oral contraceptives are steroid hormones.
questions.solution:
Estrogen and progesterone present in oral contraceptive pills are steroid hormones (lipid-derived) and are not degraded by proteolytic enzymes in the gastrointestinal tract.

In contrast, insulin is a peptide hormone. If taken orally, the peptide bonds of insulin would be broken down (digested) by proteases in the stomach and intestine, rendering it biologically inactive before it can be absorbed into the bloodstream. Therefore, it must be injected.

Answer: Insulin is a peptide hormone susceptible to digestion by gastrointestinal proteases, whereas oral contraceptives are steroid hormones.

questions.q:
Assertion : A solution of sucrose in water is dextrorotatory. But on hydrolysis in the presence of a little hydrochloric acid, it becomes laevorotatory.
Reason : Sucrose on hydrolysis gives unequal amounts of glucose and fructose. As a result of this, change in sign of rotation is observed.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
The hydrolysis of sucrose by boiling with a mineral acid $(\mathrm{HCl})$, produces a mixture of equal molecules of $D$-glucose and $D$-fructose. Sucrose solution is dextrorotatory, specific rotation $=+66.5^{\circ}$. But on hydrolysis, it becomes laevorotatory. The specific rotation of $D$-glucose is $+52^{\circ}$ and of $D$-fructose is $-92^{\circ}$. Therefore, the net specific rotation of an equimolar mixture of both is :
$\frac{+52^{\circ}-92^{\circ}}{2}=-20^{\circ}$
$\therefore \quad$ laevorotatory.

questions.solution: Latex of some plants containing long chain hydrocarbons is considered to be a good substitute for liquid fuels or petroleum. Such plants having large amount of latex with long chain hydrocarbons are called petroplants. Cultivation of petroplants is also a part of energy-cropping. Cultivation of these petrocrops was first of all done by Italians in Ethiopia about fifty years back, although actual credit for identifying the petrocrops goes to Dr. Calvin. The most common petroplants belong to families of Euphorbiaceae, Asclepiadaceae, Apocynaceae, Compositae, Labiatae, Sapotaceae, Urticaceae, etc., which have property of converting large amounts of their photosynthates into latex with hydrocarbons. Their hydrocarbon contents can be increased by genetic manipulations (genetic engineering). But commercial production of petroleum or liquid fuel alternative (through petroplants) is in early stage. The use of these petroplants may reduce the pressure on liquid fuel or petroleum.

The groups: $\mathrm{COOH}, R, \mathrm{NH}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}$ (where $R$ is an unnamed carbon chain) are arranged around the chiral center carbon atom. Sighting from the hydrogen atom, if these groups are arranged counterclockwise around the carbon atom, then it is the D-form. If clockwise, it is the L-form. questions.q: Which one of the following statements is true for protein synthesis (translation)?
options: Amino acids are directly recognized by $m$-RNA.
The third base of the codon is less specific.
Only one codon codes for an amino acid.
Every $t$-RNA molecule has more than one amino acid attachment.
questions.solution:
Genetic code shows degeneracy i.e. occurrence of more than 1 codon per amino acid. All the amino acid except methionine and tryptophan are coded by more than 1 codon.
For example, valine is specified by GUU, GUC, GUA, GUG
This shows that first two bases are common in all the four codons coding for valine. But the third base can be changed.
